kept.title: Arbitrary Code Execution in node.js via require()
kept.description: The function `loadQueries` in `node.js` uses `require.resolve` and `require` on user-controlled input (`name`), which allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code if they can influence the `name` parameter.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker creates a malicious package.
Attacker configures a `browserslist` config in a target project that points to the malicious package via `extends`.
The application calls `browserslist` for that project.
`loadQueries` invokes `require(require.resolve(name))` triggering the code.
kept.impact: Full RCE on the machine running the analysis/build process.

kept.title: Prototype Pollution via uncontrolled object copying
kept.description: While `copyObject` attempts to block specific keys, the implementation relies on a blacklist that may be bypassable or incomplete depending on the runtime environment or future object structures.
steps_to_exploit: Find an object serialization point that uses this copy function.
Inject a property name that is not in `DANGEROUS_KEYS` but allows for prototype pollution.
Manipulate the base object prototype.
kept.impact: Denial of Service or potential execution flow hijacking.

kept.title: Use of unsecure CI runner environment variable
kept.description: The workflow `test.yml` explicitly sets `ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS: true`, which re-enables deprecated and dangerous workflow commands that allow environment injection.
steps_to_exploit: Submit a PR to the project.
The CI environment will process workflows with insecure command handling enabled.
Inject malicious commands into the build output to influence the runner environment.
kept.impact: Compromise of the CI runner environment.

kept.title: Reliance on potentially malicious local config resolution
kept.description: The utility searches for configuration files (`.browserslistrc`, `package.json`) in parent directories without sufficient validation of ownership, leading to potential path traversal-like configuration loading.
steps_to_exploit: Place a malicious `.browserslistrc` in a parent directory of the project.
Execute `browserslist` from within the project structure.
The application loads the malicious config, potentially changing behavior or triggering other vulnerabilities.
kept.impact: Loading of unauthorized configurations, potentially facilitating further attacks.

kept.title: Unsafe deserialization of stats file
kept.description: The CLI and `node.js` read and parse JSON files (stats) from the filesystem provided by user arguments without schema validation.
steps_to_exploit: Create a crafted JSON file containing an deeply nested or malicious structure.
Run the CLI with `--stats=malicious.json`.
The application parses the JSON, potentially causing a crash or memory exhaustion.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) via resource exhaustion.

kept.title: Loose Semver Comparison Vulnerability
kept.description: The `semverFilterLoose` function implements custom comparison logic which may fail to correctly interpret version ranges, leading to incorrect browser selection (e.g., security-critical browser updates being ignored).
steps_to_exploit: Query for a specific version range that is ambiguous.
The loose parser incorrectly maps this to an insecure or unintended version.
The application proceeds with the wrong browser set.
kept.impact: Incorrect environment targeting, leading to security-insecure browser configurations.

kept.title: Insecure use of eval-like logic in regex
kept.description: The query parsing mechanism maps strings to function selectors via a lookup object; however, the lack of a strict allowlist for selectors poses a risk if new dynamic selectors are added.
steps_to_exploit: Inject a string that partially matches a internal key.
The query parser may misroute the call to an unintended function.
Unexpected code execution logic.

kept.title: Lack of input sanitization in `checkExtend`
kept.description: The `checkExtend` function uses regex to validate config names but does not strictly check for all potential path-injection sequences before passing them to `require.resolve`.
steps_to_exploit: Use an encoded path or unconventional characters allowed by the regex.
Bypass the prefix requirement.
Force a `require` of a local file in the project.
kept.impact: Path manipulation and potential local file disclosure/execution.

kept.title: Information Leak through error messages
kept.description: The application returns detailed error messages containing system paths and filenames when configurations fail to load.
steps_to_exploit: Provide an invalid config path.
Observe the stderr output containing the full absolute path of the failure.
Use this information for internal reconnaissance.

kept.title: Denial of Service via Cache poisoning
kept.description: The cache mechanism in `index.js` uses a stringified array as a key without limits on the length or complexity of the queries in the array, allowing memory exhaustion.
steps_to_exploit: Send many unique long queries to the `browserslist()` function.
Fill the `Map` until memory limits are reached.
The application crashes.

kept.title: Missing integrity check for dependencies
kept.description: The workflow relies on installing packages without verifying their hashes (lockfile is often ignored with `--no-frozen-lockfile` or similar).
steps_to_exploit: Compromise an upstream registry package.
The CI build automatically pulls the malicious package due to lack of lockfile enforcement.
The build output is infected.

kept.title: Insecure path calculation in `eachParent`
kept.description: Path traversal check in `pathInRoot` is weak; `path.relative` can be bypassed depending on path depth and resolution.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a project path with multiple segments.
Manipulate the `BROWSERSLIST_ROOT_PATH` environment variable.
Access configuration files outside the expected project root.

kept.title: Unsafe parsing of `package.json`
kept.description: The code uses `JSON.parse` on content read directly from disk after simple regex checks, potentially susceptible to large JSON bombs.
steps_to_exploit: Create a nested JSON structure in a dummy `package.json`.
Trigger the `parsePackage` function.
Resource exhaustion.

kept.title: Insecure temporary directory usage
kept.description: The build process uses `cleaned-project/` as a working directory in a way that might conflict with other concurrent jobs on a shared runner.
steps_to_exploit: Race condition in CI workspace.
Swap `cleaned-project` contents while the build is running.
Infect the final package.

kept.title: Exposure of environment variables in error trace
kept.description: The code uses `process.env` extensively and debug logs may contain full environmental context if a failure occurs during execution.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger a `BrowserslistError` in a environment with sensitive variables (e.g., CI).
If `BROWSERSLIST_TRACE_WARNING` is enabled, internal state including paths is dumped.
Leak of CI secrets/paths via log aggregation.
